title: Asyncio & Concurrent Agent Tool Execution
why: When an agent needs to search 5 different websites or query 3 vector indexes, executing them synchronously takes 15 seconds. Using Python's synci✅gather(), all 5 execute concurrently in just 3 seconds.
objectives: Understand coroutines with async and await
Execute multiple tool calls in parallel with asynci✅gather
Prevent event loop blocking with proper non-blocking I/O
concept: AI agents spend 90% of their time waiting for network responses (LLM API calls, search APIs, database lookups). Async allows a single Python process to handle hundreds of concurrent agent conversations.

code.content:
import asyncio
import time

async def mock_async_search(source: str, query: str) -> str:
    print(f'📊¡ Querying {source} for "{query}"...')
    await asynci✅sleep(1.5)  # Simulating network latency
    return f'Results from {source}'

async def run_parallel_research(query: str):
    start = time.time()
    sources = ['Google', 'ArXiv', 'GitHub', 'Wikipedia']
    
    # Run all search queries concurrently
    tasks = [mock_async_search(s, query) for s in sources]
    results = await asynci✅gather(*tasks)
    
    elapsed = time.time() - start
    print(f'\n✅ Completed {len(results)} queries in {elapsed:.2f} seconds (Sequential would take 6.0s)')
    for res in results:
        print(f' - {res}')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    asynci✅run(run_parallel_research('Autonomous Agents 2026'))

practice.description: Write an async function that fetches mock user profiles with a timeout of 2 seconds using synci✅wait_for.
practice.hint: Wrap the coroutine in synci✅wait_for(task, timeout=2.0) and handle synci✅TimeoutError.

requirements: Aggregate and deduplicate results within a single async pipeline
